q: Thin and flexible strips of metal used to separate sheets of drywall from the structure of the building primarily for soundproofing.
n: Resilient channels are thin, flexible metal strips that decouple drywall from the framing for soundproofing. Source: Egan, Architectural Acoustics; ASTM C645.

q: A high-rise condominium in Ortigas is experiencing wide day-to-night humidity swings due to its mixed-mode ventilation system. The developer wants a wood-finish flooring material that will maintain flatness over time, even when units are left unoccupied for weeks with no air-conditioning. The material must minimize surface distortion and movement. Which flooring option is the most appropriate for this condition?
n: Engineered wood (a cross-ply core under a veneer) stays far more dimensionally stable than solid boards through humidity swings. Source: ANSI/HPVA EF (engineered wood flooring); Philippine Wood Handbook (FPRDI-DOST); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood).

q: The Philippine Ebony is also known. as?
n: Kamagong (Diospyros blancoi) is known as Philippine ebony. Source: Philippine Wood Handbook (FPRDI-DOST); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood).

q: Which of the following is a type of Philippine Mahogany. widely recognized for its durability and strength. making ita preferred choice for construction and furniture- making?
n: Tanguile is one of the woods sold as Philippine mahogany (red lauan group), valued for durability and workability. Source: Philippine Wood Handbook (FPRDI-DOST); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood).

q: Lumber is sold units of?
n: Lumber is sold in even-numbered lengths in feet (8, 10, 12 ft...). Source: Philippine Wood Handbook (FPRDI-DOST); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood); PNS lumber standards.

q: Best way to dry lumber
n: Kiln drying is the best and most controlled way to season lumber to a target moisture content. Source: Philippine Wood Handbook (FPRDI-DOST); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood); USDA Wood Handbook, Ch. 13.

q: Which statement most accurately describes S28 lumber?
o: Surfaced on two faces, leaving the edges in their original milled state for further processing
Specially treated with chemical stabilizers to prevent warping and shrinkage
Kiln-dried and cut to exact dimensional standards, ready for installation without further machining
Underwent pressure treatment to enhance durability and resistance against moisture and decay, making it ideal for outdoor use
n: S2S lumber is surfaced (planed) on two faces only, leaving the edges rough for later processing. Source: USDA Wood Handbook, Ch. 6.

q: Which type of lumber is fully surfaces on all four sides?
n: S4S means 'surfaced four sides'. The lumber has been planed smooth on both faces and both edges, giving uniform dressed dimensions. Source: USDA Forest Products Laboratory, Wood Handbook, Ch. 6.

q: This wood joint is created by cutting a groove along one side of the board, while on the other side of the board a centered extension (tongue) is created to fit into the corresponding groove on another piece. Except for the end piece, all boards using this joint have both components cut into their edges. This joint is particularly used to create edge-to-edge joints for wide panels, floorings, sidings, wall paneling, ceilings, edging in shelving, cabinets and furniture sides. However, its most common use is for wood floorings.
n: In tongue-and-groove (T&G) joints, one edge has a groove and the other a centered tongue. They join boards edge to edge, most often in wood flooring. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood joinery); Hoadley/Fine Woodworking joinery references.

q: A carpenter is assembling quick site barricades using 2*2 framing and plywood. The boards are simply placed end-to-end and fastened together using nails. with no special shaping or joinery required. This method is commonly used for rough framing and temporary structures. What type of wood joint is being used?
n: A butt joint simply places members end to end or face to face and nails them, with no shaping. It is used for rough and temporary framing. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood joinery); Hoadley/Fine Woodworking joinery references.

q: A master carpenter is fabricating a solid-wood door frame for a boutique hotel. The joint must resist racking, handle long-term cyclical loads, and maintain structural integrity without relying on metal fasteners. The design calls for a rectangular tongue on one member inserted into a precisely cut slot on the mating piece—a traditional method used in chairs, tables, and architectural frames. Which joint best fits this description?
n: A mortise and tenon fits a rectangular tongue (tenon) into a cut slot (mortise). It resists racking in frames without metal fasteners. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood joinery); Hoadley/Fine Woodworking joinery references.

q: A foreman instructs the crew to install baseboards along a finished interior wall. At the outside corner, the two baseboard pieces must meet cleanly with a continuous profile and no exposed end grain. Which joint should be used for this type of baseboard corner?
n: Outside baseboard corners are mitered at 45° so the profile wraps continuously with no end grain showing. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood joinery); Hoadley/Fine Woodworking joinery references (finish carpentry).

q: A carpenter is installing baseboards along a long hallway where a single board is not long enough to span the entire wall. The joint between two baseboard pieces must be strong, minimize visible seams, and prevent end-grain exposure along the straight run. Which joint should be used to join the two baseboards in line?
n: In-line baseboard pieces are joined with a scarf joint, overlapping angled cuts that hide the seam and the end grain. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood joinery); Hoadley/Fine Woodworking joinery references (finish carpentry).

q: During the fabrication of custom built-in shelving for a residential study, the carpenter needs to create a joint that will securely seat each horizontal shelf into the vertical side panels. The design requires cutting a rectangular recess directly into the substrate of the side panels so that the shelves can slide in and bear weight without relying solely on fasteners, The recess must run across the grain and provide a stable housing for the shelf. Which type of joint matches this description?
n: A dado is a rectangular channel cut across the grain into a panel to seat a shelf. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood joinery); Hoadley/Fine Woodworking joinery references.

q: A renovation project for a coastal vacation house requires replacing the damaged exterior wall cladding. The architect specifies a wood siding system where each board overlaps the next through a matching edge profile that helps shed water and prevents gaps caused by expansion and contraction, The joint must be formed along the edges of the boards, not by cutting into the substrate. and should create a continuous horizontal pattern that improves weather resistance. Which type of joint satisfies this requirement?
n: Shiplap boards have rabbeted edges that overlap. This sheds water and allows movement in a continuous horizontal pattern. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood joinery); Hoadley/Fine Woodworking joinery references; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood siding).

q: A bespoke furniture shop in an upscale Makati showroom is fabricating premium solid-wood drawers for a luxury walk-in closet system. The client demands a joint that can withstand repeated pulling forces, provide exceptional mechanical strength without relying solely on glue, and showcase traditional craftsmanship. Which type of wood joint is most appropriate for constructing these high-quality drawers?
n: Dovetail joints interlock mechanically to resist pulling forces. They are the classic joint for high-quality drawers. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood joinery); Hoadley/Fine Woodworking joinery references.

q: A luxury furniture fabricator wants a cabinet with clean, seamless edges and no visible end grain at the corners. Which joinery method is most appropriate for achieving this appearance while maintaining adequate strength?
n: A miter joint reinforced with a spline hides end grain at the corner and is strong enough for cabinetry. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood joinery); Hoadley/Fine Woodworking joinery references.

q: A cabinetmaker is fabricating a series of modular drawer boxes for a built-in unit in a condominium unit located in Betis, Pampanga. The design requires the drawer back panel to fit into a recess cut along the edge of the drawer sides so that the panel sits flush while still providing a clean exterior surface. The joint must be simple to machine, allow full-length glue contact, and avoid cutting across the field of the board. Which joint is most appropriate for this condition?
n: A rabbet is a recess cut along the edge of a board. It lets a back panel sit flush, is easy to machine and gives full-length glue contact. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood joinery); Hoadley/Fine Woodworking joinery references.

q: A heritage-style renovation in Calamba requires solid wood ceiling boards to be installed in long continuous runs without visible gaps. The boards must interlock along their edges to control seasonal expansion, prevent cupping, and maintain a flush surface without relying on face nails. The architect specifies a joint that forms a projecting ridge on one board and a matching slot on the adjacent board, allowing the pieces to self-align during installation. Which joint best satisfies this requirement?
n: Tongue-and-groove boards interlock along their edges and self-align. They control movement without face nails. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood joinery); Hoadley/Fine Woodworking joinery references.

q: In this wood joint, the end of one piece of wood is inserted into a hole in another piece of wood. It is a strong and stable joint with various applications.
n: In a mortise and tenon, the end (tenon) of one piece fits into a hole (mortise) in the other. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood joinery); Hoadley/Fine Woodworking joinery references.

q: In this wood joint, channels are cut into a piece of wood but do not proceed the entire way through the thickness of the material. They are cut perpendicular to (against) the grain. The other piece is then inserted snugly into the channel. They are ideal for cabinets, shelves and a host of other applications.
n: A dado is a channel cut across the grain, part-way through the material, that receives another piece. It is used in cabinets and shelves. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood joinery); Hoadley/Fine Woodworking joinery references.

q: In this wood joint, a recess is formed at the end of a piece of wood. It matches a corresponding cut on another piece of wood with which it is paired and joined.
n: A rabbet is a recess at the edge or end of a board that matches a cut on the mating piece. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood joinery); Hoadley/Fine Woodworking joinery references.

q: A method of joinery that involves inserting a compressed wood chip into slots cut into two pieces of wood, which are then glued together.
n: A biscuit joint uses compressed wood biscuits glued into matching slots in the two pieces. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood joinery); Hoadley/Fine Woodworking joinery references.

q: A method of joinery that involves drilling a hole at an angle, usually 15 degrees, into one piece and then joining it to a second piece with a screw.
n: A pocket-hole joint uses a hole drilled at about 15° in one piece and a screw driven into the second piece. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood joinery); Hoadley/Fine Woodworking joinery references.

q: In this wood joint, a set of complementary interlocking profiles in two pieces of wood are joined (usually) at right angles and glued together. This joint does not have the same interlocking properties as a dovetail joint, but is much easier to make.
n: A box (finger) joint has interlocking rectangular fingers glued at right angles. It is easier to make than a dovetail but does not lock the same way. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood joinery); Hoadley/Fine Woodworking joinery references.

q: During the installation of wood moldings, architraves, and baseboards, the carpenter specifies a small-headed or nearly headless nail that can be driven below the wood surface to minimize visible fasteners after finishing. Which nail is most appropriate for this application?
n: Finishing nails have small, nearly headless heads that can be set below the surface and filled, for moldings and trim. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (nails).

q: The first part of a stair, it is a post found at the foot and at the top of any flight of stairs and where there is a change of direction.
n: A newel post is the main post at the foot and top of a stair flight and at changes of direction. It anchors the handrail. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (stairs).

q: Which part of a stair is designed for resting and changing direction?
n: A landing is the level platform between flights for resting and changing direction. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (stairs); NBC IRR Sec. 1207.5.e.

q: Cabinets, bookcases, kitchen island drawers, cupboards, et al. are
n: Cabinets, bookcases, kitchen islands, drawers and cupboards are casework. Source: AWI/AWMAC/WI Architectural Woodwork Standards, Sec. 10 (Casework).

q: Doors, panels, trims, moldings, et al. are
n: Doors, panels, trims and moldings are millwork. Source: AWI Architectural Woodwork Standards, Sec. 6 (Interior and Exterior Millwork).

q: Which horizontal molding is typically installed at an elevation of approximately 30 to 36 inches above the finished floor to protect walls from furniture abrasion and visually divide the wall surface?
n: A chair rail is a horizontal molding about 30–36 in. above the floor. It protects the wall from chair backs and divides the wall visually. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (moldings).

q: A decorative molding is installed at the junction of a wall and ceiling to conceal the joint while providing an elegant transition. The profile consists of a concave curve flowing into a convex curve, creating a distinctive S-shaped appearance commonly found In classical interiors. Which molding is being described?
n: An ogee molding has an S-shaped profile (concave into convex), common in classical cornices at the wall–ceiling joint. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated; Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: Which strategy best supports long-term flexibility in interior space planning?
o: Using modular partition systems with concealed service channels and standardized panel dimensions
Designing partitions with fixed finishes and embedded utilities to streamline construction sequencing
Aligning partition layout with shear cores to simplify circulation and vertical service routing
Integrating partitions with load-bearing walls to maximize acoustic and thermal performance
n: Modular demountable partitions with concealed service channels and standard panel sizes allow layouts to change over time. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (interior partitions); BIFMA demountable wall guidance.

q: Which component is commonly installed on doors and windows to reduce air leakage, improve insulation and prevent drafts, dust and moisture from entering a building?
n: Weather stripping seals door and window gaps against air leakage, drafts, dust and moisture. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (weatherstripping).

q: A component crucial for sealing the gap at the base of a door, ensuring thermal insulation, moisture resistance and a smooth transition between flooring materials. Which architectural element best fulfills this role?
n: A threshold seals the gap at the base of a door and gives a smooth transition between floor materials. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated; ANSI/BHMA A156.21 (thresholds).

q: Window with most ventilation suitable for tropical climates
n: Jalousie windows open almost fully across the opening, giving the most ventilation, which suits tropical climates. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (windows); AAMA/WDMA/CSA 101/I.S.2/A440; Lechner, Heating, Cooling, Lighting.

q: An energy-efficient residence requires an operable window with the least air infiltration when closed. Which window type is most appropriate?
n: Casement windows close by compressing onto the gaskets, giving the lowest air infiltration among operable windows. Fixed windows are not operable. Source: AAMA/WDMA/CSA 101/I.S.2/A440 (air leakage ratings).

q: Windows hinged at the sides
n: Casement windows are hinged at the side. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (windows); AAMA/WDMA/CSA 101/I.S.2/A440.

q: Windows hinged at the top
n: Awning windows are hinged at the top. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (windows); AAMA/WDMA/CSA 101/I.S.2/A440.

q: Windows hinged at the bottom
n: Hopper windows are hinged at the bottom and open inward. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (windows); AAMA/WDMA/CSA 101/I.S.2/A440.

q: Which window is easy to reach and opens or closes by turning a handle?
n: Casement windows open and close with a crank handle, easy to reach over counters. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (windows); AAMA/WDMA/CSA 101/I.S.2/A440.

q: Which window type is top-hinged, provides ventilation while protecting from rain, and is especially suitable for high or hard-to-reach locations?
n: Awning windows are top-hinged. They ventilate while shedding rain, which suits high or hard-to-reach spots. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (windows); AAMA/WDMA/CSA 101/I.S.2/A440.

q: Which window type features a vertically sliding lower sash that moves upward to allow ventilation, while the upper sash remains fixed in place?
n: A single-hung window has a lower sash that slides up while the upper sash is fixed. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (windows); AAMA/WDMA/CSA 101/I.S.2/A440.

q: Which window type allows both upper and lower sashes to slide vertically, enabling controlled ventilation and casy cleaning from the interior?
n: In a double-hung window both sashes slide vertically, allowing controlled ventilation and easy cleaning. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (windows); AAMA/WDMA/CSA 101/I.S.2/A440.

q: A residential unit has a tall and narrow wall opening intended to maximize natural ventilation in a tropical climate. The design requires a window type that can open fully, capture breezes effectively, and direct airflow into the interior. The window must function efficiently even with limited horizontal space. Which window type is most appropriate for this condition?
n: A casement opens fully and its swung sash can catch and direct breezes indoors, even in a tall, narrow opening. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (windows); AAMA/WDMA/CSA 101/I.S.2/A440; Lechner, Heating, Cooling, Lighting.

q: A narrow enclosed stairwell in a mid-rise building requires a glazed opening to introduce natural daylight into an otherwise dim circulation zone. The building's mechanical system already provides adequate ventilation, and the architect wants to avoid any operable components that could project into the limited egress width or compromise the stairwell's fire-separation rating. The window's sole function is to transmit light, and it must remain permanently closed to prevent unintended air movement between floors. Which window type is most appropriate for this condition?
n: A fixed window lets in daylight with no operable parts. It stays closed and keeps the stairwell's separation intact. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (windows); AAMA/WDMA/CSA 101/I.S.2/A440; RIRR of RA 9514 (exit enclosure openings).

q: 4 glazed opening installed directly on the roof surface is primarily used to introduce natural daylight into interior spaces that have limited access to exterior walls. What is this feature called'?
n: A skylight is glazing set in the roof to daylight interior spaces. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: Which architectural feature best supports direct serving and casual interaction between a kitchen and an adjacent outdoor dining area?
o: Sliding glass door with full-panel operability and integrated insect screen
Pass-through window with counter extending from the kitchen to the exterior
Folding glass wall system with flush floor track for seamless transition
Retractable awning window above a fixed counter surface
n: A pass-through window with a counter extending outside allows direct serving between the kitchen and outdoor dining. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (kitchen planning).

q: Which of the following does NOT typically characterize French windows?
o: Opens in the middle to form a full-height opening
n: French windows are tall, largely glazed, and open in the middle to full height. They are not typically known for energy efficiency. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (windows); AAMA/WDMA/CSA 101/I.S.2/A440.
